chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleyman ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the seed (nutfah) is twenty dinars, and regarding the clot (alaqah) is forty dinars, and regarding the lump (mudghah) is sixty dinars, and regarding the bones (azam) is eighty dinars. So when the flesh covers it, it is a hundred dinars. Then it is its wergild (diyah) until it commences (breathing/crying). So when it commences, the wergild is complete.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a fetus at different stages of development in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a progressive scale of blood money (diyah) for fetal homicide, correlating the compensation with specific stages of embryonic development as understood in classical Islamic jurisprudence. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the transition from partial to full liability occurs at 'istihlal' (the first breath or cry), marking the fetus as a distinct legal person entitled to complete inheritance and compensation rights.
